task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-270's marker insertion across 13 lib/letflow/design/ files, with rigorous byte-level scrutiny of the novel list-item-merge technique that produced 14 deletions -- unprecedented in this chunk series.

result.note: Independently re-derived, not trusted from DOC-UPDATER's report. (1) Scope: `git diff 0d245925..HEAD --stat` shows exactly the 13 target files plus handoffs/ jsons -- 111 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-) confirmed; `git diff --stat -- . ':!lib/letflow/design' ':!handoffs'` returns empty, so CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/migration/README.md and every design file outside this chunk are untouched. (2) List-item-merge technique, byte-diffed on req182, req185, req188, req197 (all 6 instances), req198 (both), req202 (both): in every case the marker text 'PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):' replaces only the bullet/number's leading content, and the ORIGINAL citation text (including bold markers, inline code, punctuation) reappears on the immediately following line(s) at the same indentation the list marker's width already establishes -- character-for-character identical to the pre-change text, confirmed by reading full diff hunks. No text was truncated, reworded, or duplicated. (3) Numbering safety: req188 and req197 (OQ items 1/1 patterns) and req182 both have numbered-list instances ('1.', '2.') -- spot-checked req188 item 1 against item 2 in the same list (lines 16-34): both use identical 3-space continuation indent, confirming the file's own pre-existing list-continuation convention, and no renumbering was needed or performed because no new list item was inserted -- the marker became the existing item's own first line, item numbers 1/2/etc. are unchanged before and after. Bulleted ('-') instances behave identically with 2-space continuation matching surrounding bullets. (4) Blockquote cases (req178, req192): both use '> PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):' as a new first line inside the existing blockquote, preserving '>' prefix syntax -- consistent with REQ-269/req151's approved precedent, no new deviation. (5) Table case (req197, section 9 and section 11): confirmed exactly one standalone marker line inserted immediately above each table's header row (not per-row, not inside the table), matching the design's explicit table-unit rule and prior-chunk precedent. (6) Per-file `.zig` line counts independently regrepped before (git show 0d245925:<file> | grep -c '\.zig') vs after (grep -c '\.zig' <file>) for all 13 files: identical per file, totals 37=37 -- the 14 deletions are pure reformatting of the same citation lines, zero citations lost, none duplicated. (7) `grep -rnE 'unlike R-Co|deliberately diverges|diverges from R-Co'` re-run against both 0d245925 and HEAD across all 13 files: single hit in both, req194-prometheus-metrics.md, same text, only line number shifted 420->421 due to one inserted marker earlier in the file -- byte-identical text confirmed. (8) No YAML frontmatter (`---` as first line) in any of the 13 files. All eight independent verification points match DOC-UPDATER's own claims and, more importantly, hold up under direct byte-level diff inspection. The novel list-item-merge technique is judged SAFE: it is a correct, idempotent-compatible application of the design's paragraph/line-unit rule (marker becomes the unit's leading line) applied to a list item as its enclosing unit, rather than a new technique invented ad hoc -- no Markdown list semantics were broken, no renumbering occurred or was needed since no new items were added, and every citation's original prose is preserved verbatim as a continuation line. No REVIEWER findings requiring rework.
